children: Australian equities were flat on Monday, as gains in banks were offset by sharp losses in gold stocks, which slid after U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish comments fuelled U.S. rate-hike hopes and dented demand for the non-yielding metal.

Last week's data showed consumer prices rose more than expected, prompting investors to shift their expectations from a pause at the Reserve Bank of Australia's September meeting to a 25-basis-point rate hike.
lost as much as 4.2%, set to mark their worst session in over a month and leading losses on the benchmark index. Bullion prices weakened, as investors reacted to Warsh's remarks.

Speaking at the Fed's annual economic symposium in Jackson Hole, Warsh said the U.S. central bank would "have work to do" if policymakers were not confident that underlying inflation was returning to its 2% target.
Gold miner Northern Star announced the appointment of Phillip Coetzer as acting chief financial officer.
